sets.name: screen registry — screen_id + screen_name
sets.note: THE SCREEN DICTIONARY. Every screen gets a row here BEFORE its ticket is written, and both values come from this row — never typed at a call site. screen_id is the stable key: snake_case, assigned once, never edited and never re-used, so a rename never breaks a saved funnel. screen_name is the human label, in the ticket’s own words, and is what a person searches for in the analytics tool; it may be edited when the screen is renamed, and the id stays put. Decided 7 Sep 2026 (decision 27): the shipped labels are kept verbatim, casing included — nothing is renamed.

The OS sheet it raises is not a screen and gets no row — it is measured by permission_os_sheet_shown / permission_result. naming_rules: screen_name: "<Flow> - <Screen>", the flow prefix taken from the epic and the screen in the words the ticket uses. Readable at a glance in a long analytics dropdown, and it sorts by flow.
screen_id: snake_case of the same words, prefixed by flow. Assigned once. If a screen is renamed, the label changes and the id does not.
One row per screen, not per state. A screen with ten states is one screen_id carrying a state property (see ConnectSSO).
A screen with no row has no ticket. If the row is missing, add it here first — that is the step that stops an event name being invented.

The two embrace bridges are TWO screens, not two states of one — they sit at different points in the flow and carry different copy. They share a shell and a variant value set (§16); they do not share a screen_id. Added 9 Sep 2026, before the Profile 05 ticket was written.

A bridge screen is a screen but NOT a step. profile_embrace_build has a row here and deliberately has no row in §2 — firing profile_step_viewed on it would put a phantom step in the completion funnel.

ProfilePhotos is step 1 of a DIFFERENT group ("The real you"), not a fifth step of "The basics". Its step_index is 1 within that group; §2 also records that photos sits outside the Share-some-details progress bar. Two progress bars, two vocabularies — do not renumber one against the other.

The photos screen's PERMISSION states have no events yet. A card-shown / mode / granted / refused / returned-from-settings set must be defined in events.json (with a closed access_status value set here) BEFORE the Profile 06 sprint — flagged 9 Sep 2026. Until then the screen's most likely drop-off point is invisible.

Profile 06 requests NO library permission (system picker on iOS and Android 13+), so the library access card is Android ≤ 12 only and there is no limited-access state at all. Any access_status value set defined later must cover the CAMERA (both platforms, always) and the old-Android library case — not an iOS library status, which we never read.

sets.name: prompt length_bucket
sets.note: Bucketed answer length on prompt_saved, and draft length on prompt_editor_dismissed (which adds "0" for an untouched field). NEVER SEND THE ANSWER TEXT — it is user-written free text about themselves, destined for a public profile, and it has no business in the analytics pipeline. The buckets exist to answer one question: did framing the field with a floor (“One good sentence is enough”) instead of a 0/160 ceiling move what people write. Boundaries are inclusive and tied to the 160 cap; if the cap changes, these change with it. Added 13 Sep 2026 with the Profile 07 ticket.

sets.name: media_prompt_id registry
sets.note: THE MEDIA PROMPT DICTIONARY. Separate from prompt_topic_id (§17) and topic_id (§6) — those are the written prompts on the profile; these are the eleven things a person can say in ten or fifteen seconds. STORE AND SEND THE ID, NEVER THE DISPLAY STRING: the prompts are copy, they will be edited, and an edit must not orphan the clips recorded under them. Position is the order the list renders and is fixed; own_idea is always last and always carries is_own_prompt: true. The SAME eleven are offered for video and for voice — nothing in the id says which, so type is required on every event that carries one. preview_on marks the prompt shown on an empty card, per medium, which is the one the user sees before opening the list. Carried by media_prompt_selected, video_recording_started, voice_recording_started, video_prompt_recorded, voice_prompt_recorded, media_review_shown, media_retaken and media_deleted. Added 16 Sep 2026 with the Media screens pass. Source of truth for the display strings: ui_kits/show-up/screens-profile-media.jsx → MEDIA_PROMPTS + MEDIA_PROMPT_OWN. FROM 16 SEP 2026 THE CARD PREVIEW IS RANKED, NOT FIXED (decision 33): the prompt shown on each empty card is the most-completed prompt for that medium, published by the server, and the preview_on column below is only the cold-start fallback used until the sample is large enough. Position stays fixed — the LIST order does not move, only the preview does; a list that reorders itself makes a user who came back for row 7 hunt for it.

sets.note: On media_screen_viewed and media_prompt_ranking_published. ranked means the previewed prompt came from the completion ranking; fallback means the ranking had no publishable answer — under the minimum sample, a new market, or the job has not run — and the cold-start prompt in §20 was shown. sets.name: sheet dismiss_method
sets.note: THE CANONICAL SHEET-CLOSE VOCABULARY, and the only one: every bottom sheet in the product reports its dismissal with these four values. Carried by prompt_editor_dismissed, prompt_topic_list_dismissed and media_prompt_list_dismissed, and by every sheet added after them. close is the X or a Cancel control; backdrop is a tap on the scrim; swipe is the drag-down gesture; system_back is the Android gesture or hardware key, which is NOT the same act as the X and must not be folded into it (decision 32). Created 16 Sep 2026 by unifying three drifted spellings of the same four acts — close|scrim|swipe|back on the prompts write sheet and cancel|backdrop|swipe|system_back on the media prompt list. Neither had shipped, so nothing in the warehouse needed migrating; a sheet-close value outside this set is a bug at the call site. Never use the key method for this (§8): method already means phone · apple · google.

sets.name: permission_status
sets.note: THE OS PERMISSION STATE, for every permission in §8's type set. Four values, one vocabulary across both platforms: not_determined (never asked — the only state in which our own sheet can be raised), granted, denied (includes 'permanently denied' — the distinction is the platform's rationale flag, which is a BEHAVIOUR branch, not a second value), restricted (parental controls / MDM; treated as denied everywhere in the product). Carried by permission_status_changed as from and to. NOT a consent: consent is §8 channel and lives on our server, this is the device's answer and is re-read on every foreground rather than remembered. limited is deliberately absent — it is a photo-library concept and stays on permission_result's own type. Android <= 12 notifications have no runtime permission at all and are reported as granted. Created 21 Sep 2026 with the Profile 09 ticket.
